Noo-Noo Disk Guardian — Founding Wave

Status: WAVE COMPLETE — reviewed, fixed-in-place, graded A- (debrief at the bottom). 4 of 5 slices built and review-hardened on final -r branches awaiting the lead's merge train (sizer → audit-ledger → leaks-r → offload-r); velocity honestly stalled on unmerged deps, re-dispatch next wave. [2026-07-15 review correction: the earlier "BUILDING" status below sections reflects mid-wave state; the gate hardened from plain go test to go test -race per charter D12.]

The wish (verbatim)

(1) "Our greatest problem on this computer is that it has like only 25gb free — but for some reason this is constantly getting eaten up by system or something else — can you do an analysis on what is clogging this system — it is really annoying because it doesn't care that i am deleting — it is for some reason still filling it up."

(2) "We have supporting harddrives which we want to utilize for anything that takes up space — main drive should be as clean as possible."

(3) "Please run an epic cycle on solving this — maybe copy down our project named noo-noo and make this provide a permanent fix on issues like these (https://github.com/FRIKKern/noo-noo)."

(4) "If we can figure out ways to offload — then we do that — if not — we might have to schedule cleanup based on how fast it clutters — or disable functionality fully so our mac does not crash from lack of harddrive space."

What the diagnosis already proved (2026-07-15 session)

  • 228G internal APFS; Data volume was 167G used / 15G free.
  • Smoking gun: /private/var/folders/…/X/com.google.Chrome.code_sign_clone/ held 65 leaked Chrome code-sign clones, du-reported ~2G each (129G total). Chrome leaks one per crash/force-kill.
  • Critical lesson: deleting 64 of them freed only ~3G — they are APFS copy-on-write clones sharing blocks. Naive du lies catastrophically. Any tool in this space MUST size APFS-clone-aware (real unique allocated blocks), or every suggestion is fiction.
  • Remaining real usage: ~/Library 56G (LocalWP 17G, Claude 11G, Google 5.5G, discord 2.2G, Caches 12G, pnpm 4.2G), ~/.colima 13G, ~/.claude 8.2G, ~/.npm 5.7G, ~/.nvm 3.9G, ~/actions-runner 3.3G, ~/go 2.7G, /opt 10G, /private/var/db 4.7G.
  • External drives: /Volumes/SATECHI (1.8T, 1.7T free) and /Volumes/Kompis.
  • Quick regenerable-cache wins already executed this session (go-build, pip, ShipIt, npm cache).
  • Open hypothesis for "deleting doesn't free": local APFS/Time Machine snapshots pinning deleted blocks — survey must check tmutil listlocalsnapshots + purgeable space.

Direction — the bold bet for this wave

Finished experience: the Mac never silently fills again. The menubar shows real reclaimable bytes (clone-aware, never du-fiction). When a known leak class recurs — Chrome code_sign_clone first — the daemon names it within one pressure cycle and offers the one-click, evidence-cited fix. Bulky-but-loved assets (LocalWP sites, colima VM, package stores) live on SATECHI behind symlinks, moved by a policy-driven offload module with per-asset safety playbooks and volume-present guards. Whatever can't be offloaded gets a velocity-derived cleanup cadence; whatever can't be cleaned gets an honest "cap or disable this" suggestion. All of it rides noo-noo's existing safety philosophy: diagnose by default, destructive actions gated, audited.

Tentative key choices (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds):

  1. Truth first. Build an APFS-clone-aware + sparse-aware sizing primitive (a sizer package reporting real-unique-allocated bytes) and make it THE size source for every module. This is the foundation slice — without it pillars (a), (c), (d) all lie. The 129G→3G incident is the proof.
  2. Ride the existing Module contract. New capabilities are modules/extensions of internal/modules.Module (Scan/Plan/Apply) — no parallel architecture. A new relocate action kind (move+symlink) joins delete, gated exactly like destructive actions.
  3. Leak signatures as data. A registry of named signatures (path pattern + evidence + safe-fix + upstream cause), scanning /private/var/folders and sibling hidden system areas. Chrome code_sign_clone is signature #1. New signatures are one registry entry, not new code.
  4. Offload playbooks per asset class. LocalWP, colima, pnpm/npm/nvm stores, actions-runner, go — each with move+symlink tolerance knowledge, native-relocation alternatives where the app supports it, and hard guards (volume UUID pinned, mount-present, never dangling).
  5. Velocity-based scheduling extends the existing 0.5 pressure package: per-asset-class growth rate measured into the store, cleanup cadence proportional to fill rate.
  6. Last-resort disable/cap suggestions (Chrome relaunch hygiene, colima disk cap) as RiskHigh advisory actions — never auto.
  7. Chase the "deleting doesn't free" ghost to ground. If APFS snapshots/purgeable space are pinning blocks, snapshot awareness becomes part of the truth pillar.

Priority within the wave: truth sizing (b) and leak-signature scanning (a) are the heart; offload (c) is the biggest user win; velocity (d) and disable-suggestions (e) complete the wish but can be thin v1s.

Survey plan (in flight now)

15 Sonnet surveyors, cast wide. Each question + why it changes the plan:

  1. repo-architecture — Map daemon/CLI/menubar architecture: module registration, scan orchestration, IPC, config, launchd. Why: every slice must plug into the real seams, not imagined ones.
  2. sizing-truth — How sizes are computed today; what macOS/Go APIs give clone-aware/sparse-aware real bytes (fcntl F_LOG2PHYS, statfs, snapshot APIs, diskutil). Why: decides feasibility + design of the foundation slice.
  3. leak-scan-surface — Structure/permissions of /private/var/folders (C/T/X classes); what's reachable without root/Full Disk Access; TCC. Why: scoping the leak scanner's reach and its permission story.
  4. chrome-leak-signature — The code_sign_clone leak: trigger conditions, upstream bug state, safe-deletion rules while Chrome runs. Why: signature #1 must be correct and safe.
  5. snapshot-ghost — On THIS machine: tmutil local snapshots, purgeable space, APFS snapshot pinning — does deleting-not-freeing reproduce? Why: may be the real answer to wish (1); reshapes the truth pillar.
  6. offload-playbooks — Per-asset move+symlink tolerance: LocalWP, colima VM, pnpm/npm/nvm, actions-runner, go, node_modules; native relocation options; known pitfalls. Why: the playbook registry's initial content and safety claims.
  7. external-volumes — Filesystems/free/mount behavior of SATECHI + Kompis; guards needed (UUID pinning, mount-wait, sleep/eject behavior). Why: relocation guard design; exFAT vs APFS changes what may live there.
  8. pressure-velocity — internal/pressure + heuristics/cache_velocity: what velocity measurement and time-series storage already exist. Why: pillar (d) should extend, not duplicate.
  9. autoclean-gates — The 0.5 auto-clean multi-gate design + audit trail. Why: relocate/delete actions must honor the same philosophy; find reusable gate code.
  10. module-contract — Module/Action/Apply/Result flow across dev/caches/startup modules. Why: what changes a relocate action kind actually needs.
  11. menubar-cli-surface — How suggestions render in Wails menubar + CLI + notify. Why: new asset classes and leak alerts must surface somewhere users see.
  12. bp-ledger-prior-art — Barkpark papers/tasks mentioning noo-noo/disk/cleanup; noo-noo docs/plans roadmap. Why: don't re-plan what a phase plan already settles; find the epic task if any.
  13. system-clutter-map — Beyond the known list: what else eats this disk (swap/VM, iOS backups, Xcode, /private/var/db, Claude 11G?). Why: asset-class registry completeness; Claude/LocalWP entries are big and unexamined.
  14. daemon-scheduling — Daily tick + pressure-scan orchestration; where per-class velocity cadences hook in. Why: pillar (d) attachment point.
  15. store-metrics — internal/store + metrics schema for history/audit. Why: velocity time series and signature-hit history need persistence.

Ledger

Epic parent task: none exists yet — Decide files it (with wave_paper pointing here). Slice tasks: filed at Decide, each linking this Paper. Wave phases append below: Digest (survey digest + verify plan), Decide (decisions + wave plan), Review (debrief).

Digest — survey digest + verify plan (2026-07-15, 15 reports in)

Status: DIGESTED — verify fleet in flight. Next append: Decide (decisions + wave plan).

What is now established

  • The "deleting doesn't free" ghost is SOLVED — and it is not snapshots. Time Machine has no destination configured; the Data volume (disk3s5) has ZERO APFS snapshots; the only 3 snapshots on the machine are sealed OS-update snapshots on the System volume. Snapshot-pinning is disconfirmed on this Mac. The real ghost is two-headed: (1) APFS copy-on-write clones making du lie (founding 129G→3G proof), and (2) continuous REFILL — newly discovered: /private/tmp holds 24G of unpurged agent/build scratch (claude-501/ 4.6G + dozens of 200–950M Barkpark worker gocache dirs, 7354/7357 entries user-owned, macOS never cleans it). Snapshot awareness stays as a cheap informational check for other machines, not a pillar.
  • Truth sizing is feasible and PROVEN on this machine. noo-noo's only sizer, core.DirSize (walk.go:11-34), sums logical st_size — not even du-equivalent. Both du and st_blocks report full size per clone (proven with a controlled cp -c case). fcntl(F_LOG2PHYS_EXT) works from Go — with one real ABI gotcha: struct log2phys is #pragma pack(4) (20 bytes; Go's natural layout is 24 and silently misaligns — hand-marshal a raw buffer). The prototype detected full clone-sharing AND partial CoW-divergence correctly. golang.org/x/sys is already a dep. Two-tier design confirmed: v1 = statfs before/after delta (real bytes freed, cheap, immediate); v2 = extent-dedup prediction (proven mechanism, unbenchmarked at scale). Bonus proof of sparse-awareness need: colima's disk is 20G apparent / 1.1G real.
  • Chrome signature #1 is fully specified. Path glob /private/var/folders/*/*/X/*.code_sign_clone/code_sign_clone.??????; created by Chromium's CodeSignCloneManager (all Chromium browsers affected); leaked on crash/force-kill (cleanup is a post-exit helper that never runs). mtime is an unsafe heuristic — the one clone on this machine is 6 days old yet held open by 7 live Chrome processes. Correct staleness test: lsof +D <leaf> returns zero rows (lsof error/timeout = do-not-delete). Upstream "fixed in 133" is false (this machine: Chrome 149, 65 leaks).
  • The Safety gate BLOCKS the flagship fix. core.Safety.CanDelete hard-codes /private/ in alwaysBlocked (safety.go:38) — every code_sign_clone lives there. Without a deliberate narrow carve-out (or a parallel predicate gated on lsof-empty), the signature can diagnose but never Apply. Also: README claims a "not a symlink out" guard that the code does not implement; and relocate needs a NEW two-sided predicate (destination UUID-pinned, mount-present, write-probed) — CanDelete cannot express it.
  • Three parallel action paths, no single choke point. modules.Action (Scan/Plan/Apply) drives ONLY the on-demand CLI; the daemon/menubar/auto-clean run on heuristics.Suggestion (no Op, no SizeBytes field) and autoclean.Action (own Deleter map, only "dev" registered). The menubar suggestions submenu is built and tested but DISCONNECTED (main.go passes nil — "Task 57" never done); notify's deepLink is dead code. Any slice that should reach the menubar/one-click UX must wire the heuristics path, not just a Module.
  • Velocity measurement exists but is DEAD in production. The whole vertical (cache_size_history schema → RecordCacheSize → scanCaches → CacheVelocity heuristic) is implemented and green-tested, but config.ScanCfg has no cache-roots field and both scan.ScanRoots call sites pass Caches: nil — zero rows ever recorded. The pillar-(d) fix starts as one config field + two call sites, then: real-rate math (current = 2-point ratio, no time normalization), per-asset-class thresholds (current = one global pair), sizer-truth collection (current = naive walk). Cadence must ride the existing single-consumer trig channel / heuristic self-gating — a second timer goroutine would break the only scan-storm guard. Related dead code: config.PressureCfg is defined but never read (thresholds hardcoded); TriggerManual/TriggerScan is a stub.
  • Autoclean's gate cascade is reusable as-is (master switch → risk-ack → module allowlist → idle days → min size; budget; daily-only enforced twice; audit pre-row before delete). Known gap: the CLI kill-switch Toggle persists in-memory only (save callback nil) — reverts on daemon restart.
  • Offload playbook surprises. pnpm store-dir is ALREADY on SATECHI (model precedent — native config beats symlinks where it exists). LocalWP's 17G is NOT site data: 15G is blueprints/ (template cache; ~/Local Sites is empty) — likely delete-class, not offload-class. Native env-var relocation exists for go (GOPATH), nvm (NVM_DIR), npm cache; unverified for colima (COLIMA_HOME) and ~/.claude. New relocate candidates: Claude vm_bundles/claudevm.bundle 10G (VM-disk class, same as colima). New small leak signatures: Electron stale app versions (discord app-0.0.395+397), actions-runner bin.2.334.0/externals cruft, pnpm .tools.
  • External volumes: one good, one broken, one live warning. SATECHI: APFS, 1.9T free, UUID 0DBD1B63-…, rw — real target. Kompis is mounted READ-ONLY right now (cause unknown) — a live counterexample to "mounted = usable"; guards must write-probe, not trust flags. Both mount noowners (permission-sensitive assets need per-asset playbooks). And the user has ALREADY hand-rolled the exact failure mode the epic prevents: ~/Desktop, ~/Documents, ~/Downloads are unguarded symlinks straight into /Volumes/SATECHI — a standing dangling-risk noo-noo should detect and report.
  • Store: one contradiction to resolve (see verify), plus no retention anywhere. migrations/0005_auto_clean_events.sql is fully designed but NOT in schema.sql (the only schema applied; currentSchemaVersion=1), and *store.Store implements none of RecordAutoCleanEvent/UpdateAutoCleanEvent/AutoCleanStatsSince — yet the autoclean engine and tick.go's sqlEventStore adapter depend on them. Either the adapter papers over it or autoclean errors at runtime. Also: cache_size_history and actions grow unbounded — new time-series tables must ship with pruning, or noo-noo's own store becomes a disk-bloat source.
  • Clean slate confirmed. Full 1415-task ledger sweep + search: zero prior noo-noo art beyond this wave's own Paper+tag. noo-noo's roadmap stops at shipped 0.5.0; none of this epic's slices were ever planned. No epic parent task exists yet — Decide files it. (Near-miss to reconcile at Decide: the old backlog's "Time Machine integration" item vs. this wave's snapshot check.)

Contradictions / course corrections vs. the Strategize direction

  • Snapshot hypothesis (key choice #7): disconfirmed — demote to a cheap informational signature; the truth pillar is clones + sparse files + refill velocity.
  • "Ride the Module contract" (key choice #2) is necessary but NOT sufficient — the daemon/menubar UX the direction promises runs on the heuristics/autoclean paths, which are Op-less and size-less. Decide must scope which path each slice wires, or builders under-deliver (CLI-visible, menubar-invisible).
  • LocalWP moves from offload column to cleanup column (blueprints cache), pending a regenerability check.
  • Audit-events contradiction: autoclean-gates report describes the audit trail as live; store-metrics proves the table/methods don't exist in the store package. Verifier will settle it with runtime evidence.
  • /private/tmp joins the leak-scan scope (24G, bigger than any single Library asset) — with an in-use guard so noo-noo never deletes a live agent scratchpad.

Coverage map — checked and NOT found (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

Checked, found, evidence-anchored: module seam + registration (module.go, report_cmd.go, *_cmd.go); daemon tick/scheduler/pressure fan-in (main.go, tick.go, watch.go); IPC namespaces (server.go, protocol.go); config load/defaults (config.go); launchd plist; autoclean gates/budget/audit design (config.go, apply.go, budget.go, 0005 sql); heuristics + cache_size_history vertical; store schema + APIs; menubar/CLI/notify surfaces incl. the disconnected submenu; core safety + DirSize; live host: /private/var/folders permissions incl. Data-Vault EPERM leaves, /private/tmp census, /private/var/db, ~/Library breakdowns (Claude 11G = 10G VM bundle; Google; discord), external volume facts, snapshot state, Chrome clone liveness via lsof, F_LOG2PHYS_EXT prototype runs.

Checked and NOT found (confirmed absences): no clone/sparse/APFS-aware sizing code anywhere; no leak-signature concept; no process-liveness helper (lsof/pgrep); no relocate/UUID-pinning/symlink-creation code; no working rollback precedent (startup.restoreLog is dead code); no retention/pruning/VACUUM in store; no cache-roots config field (velocity dead); cfg.Pressure never read; auto_clean_events absent from applied schema; no MobileSync backups or Xcode on this machine; no prior Barkpark art.

Corners NO surveyor reached (named honestly): internal/scan/repos.go (never opened); autoclean/ipc/cli test bodies + test/e2e/autoclean_gates_test.go internals; Wails frontend generated bindings (models.ts) and Settings.svelte line-by-line; internal/audit/audit.go (call-site level only); /var/folders/zz/* daemon-account contents (likely root-only); TCC-gated ~/Library paths (Mail/Photos/Messages); whether Full Disk Access lifts the Data-Vault EPERM; F_LOG2PHYS_EXT cost at scale and behavior on Chrome-owned files; macOS orphan-clone reaping on reboot; clean-quit→lsof-empty race window.

Verify plan — the LAST look before Decide (6 assignments, in flight)

  1. sizer-live-proof (opus, RUNS) — re-run the F_LOG2PHYS_EXT prototype against the live Chrome code_sign_clone leaf under /private/var/folders (permission context unproven); benchmark extent-walk wall-clock on a large many-file tree (LocalWP blueprints ~15G, a node_modules tree); extent-dedup 2–3 /private/tmp gocache dirs to test whether the 24G du figure is clone-inflated. Proof = actual program output + timings.
  2. autoclean-events-ledger (opus, RUNS) — settle the 0005 contradiction: read tick.go:200-243 sqlEventStore; inspect the live store.db tables (sqlite3 .tables); run go test ./internal/autoclean/... ./internal/store/... + the e2e gates test; determine whether an armed autoclean would error at runtime today. Also confirm Toggle save=nil consequence.
  3. gates-baseline (sonnet, RUNS) — prove the build/test gates pass on noo-noo main before any builder flies: CC=/usr/bin/clang go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... — including whether cmd/noo-noo-app (Wails) builds locally and whether frontend bindings regen is part of the loop. Record duration + flakes.
  4. safety-velocity-probe (sonnet, worktree, RUNS) — probe tests proving (a) Safety.CanDelete rejects a /private/var/folders path today (pins the fail-before state for the carve-out task), and (b) wiring scan.Roots{Caches:[tmpdir]} genuinely lights the dead velocity pipeline end-to-end (rows recorded, CacheVelocity fires on seeded growth) — the claimed one-config-field fix, proven not assumed.
  5. offload-native-unknowns (sonnet, RUNS) — pnpm: config get store-dir + PNPM_HOME actual values; colima: does COLIMA_HOME exist (binary/help/docs) and must the VM be stopped; ~/.claude: any data-dir override (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR etc.); LocalWP: are blueprints regenerable (docs); Electron-symlink tolerance evidence. Output = per-asset verdict table for the playbook registry.
  6. volume-guard-facts (sonnet, RUNS) — why is Kompis read-only and is it user-recoverable (diagnose only, no remount without consent); SATECHI UUID/mount facts via diskutil info -plist; live write-probe both volumes; confirm the Desktop/Documents/Downloads symlink risk report for the guard spec.

Held for Decide (not verifiable cheaply, or design calls): the /private/ carve-out shape (narrow allowlist vs parallel predicate); which action path (module vs heuristic vs autoclean) each slice wires; per-asset-class taxonomy shared by velocity + leak registry + playbooks; retention policy for new tables; whether to fix cfg.Pressure dead-wiring opportunistically; /private/tmp claude-501 in-use guard design.

Verification results (deep round — Decide, 2026-07-15)

Six verifiers ran with live proofs. Trust order held: proofs > facts > prose. Summary per assignment, decisive lines quoted:

  • sizer-live-proof — PROVEN, with an architecture correction. F_LOG2PHYS_EXT extent-union works on the live Chrome clone with zero permission surprises: files=943 ferrs=0 elapsed=74.2ms — blocks=2.00GB, UNIQUE-ALLOCATED=1.99GB. Founding incident reproduced in a controlled cp -c pair: du 400M … COMBINED unique=200.00MB, shared/saved=200.00MB; diverging 50M dropped shared to exactly 150M (extent-level granularity). Cross-tree CoW sharing detected: clone vs updated /Applications Chrome = shared 677.06MB. COST decides the role: ~/.npm (197,761 files) took 6.72s (~34µs/file) → extent-union is a SCOPED precision instrument, not the everywhere-size (→ D1 truth-tiering). TWO digest assumptions refuted: blueprints is ONE 14.84GB file (Polyflor.zip), not a many-file tree; the /private/tmp gocaches share 0B — the 24G there is HONEST distinct data, dedup conjures nothing. Hardening: extents MUST be keyed by (st_dev, devoffset); hardlink sums need inode-dedup.
  • autoclean-events-ledger — CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: 0005 is NOT a blocker. The pivot both surveyors missed: cmd/noo-nood/main.go:366 applyAutoCleanMigration inlines the 0005 DDL at daemon boot (log.Fatal on failure). Write path works via tick.go's sqlEventStore adapter; Apply fail-safes (audit pre-delete abort BEFORE os.RemoveAll). The REAL gaps: read path dead (NewAutoCleanService(&acSnap, nil, nil) — Status always 0), toggle save=nil (restart reverts), DDL duplicated with store.Open consumers table-less. NOT-FOUND: live store.db absent (daemon never ran here — fresh clone, expected). Gate baseline GREEN. Caveat: the assignment's -run 'AutoClean|Store' filter matched ZERO tests (false-empty) — unfiltered suites are the real proof.
  • gates-baseline — GREEN at b6b9644. go build ./... exit 0 (Wails app links; benign ld version warnings), go vet exit 0, go test ./... 19/19 ok, and the REAL Makefile gate go test -race ./... also fully green (~38s, zero races). NOT-FOUND: no go:embed and no frontend/dist — plain go build never touches the Svelte frontend (→ D14: menubar UI is a separate toolchain surface). internal/modules has zero direct tests.
  • safety-velocity-probe — BOTH CLAIMS PROVEN. (a) Fail-before pinned: CanDelete rejects the Chrome clone path even when explicitly allowlisted — alwaysBlocked (safety.go:38 /private/) is checked BEFORE caller roots, so the carve-out cannot be an allowlist entry (→ D4 parallel predicate). (b) One config field lights the dead velocity pipeline end-to-end: ScanRoots with Caches:[dir] wrote 1 cache_size_history row … CacheVelocity fired: "10.0x growth in 7d" risk=medium. Gotchas recorded: store.Open needs a real file path; same-second samples need a backdated baseline row. Probe test files were verified then trashed (main checkout kept clean) — builders re-author from the recipes in the tasks.
  • offload-native-unknowns — ALL 5 VERDICTS CLOSED; one digest hypothesis REFUTED. pnpm store-dir is NOT globally pinned (home-cwd → internal 4.3G store, SATECHI-cwd → external 6.1G store — proven by running pnpm store path from both volumes); colima natively supports COLIMA_HOME (string in the installed binary); Claude Code natively supports CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (string in the real binary the wrapper execs). LocalWP blueprints is NOT delete-class: it is ONE user-created 14.8G Blueprint; official docs: "If you delete a Blueprint file, it is permanently lost—there's no automatic regeneration." An auto-clean built on the digest's hypothesis would have destroyed irreplaceable client data → NEVER-delete flag is law. NOT-FOUND: no native blueprints-path config; no Electron userData symlink precedent on this machine (tolerance genuinely unverified → smoke-test gate, no blanket assumption).
  • volume-guard-facts — GUARD LAW GROUNDED IN A LIVE COUNTEREXAMPLE. Kompis is read-only from REAL APFS corruption: "The volume /dev/rdisk5s1 … was found to be corrupt and needs to be repaired" (fsck non-destructive) — mounted+parseable ≠ usable; only a live write-probe is ground truth (touch /Volumes/Kompis/... → Read-only file system, SATECHI probe passed). UUIDs pinned: SATECHI 0DBD1B63-0377-450B-A340-7E72D0925EBC, Kompis DE891A7A-…. The user's hand-rolled ~/Desktop, ~/Documents, ~/Downloads → SATECHI symlinks confirmed unguarded (dangling-ENOENT failure proven by simulation; Downloads holds live recent data). NOT-FOUND: no diskarbitrationd log lines within the 24h buffer; no prior volume-guard code in noo-noo. Kompis remediation (repairVolume) deliberately NOT run — needs backup + user consent (backlog nn-bl-volume-health).

Decisions (mirror of the charter — canonical: barkpark .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-epic-charter.md, commit d3771c0)

  • D1 Truth-tiering: st_blocks cheap default; extent-union scoped to clone dirs/offload candidates — proven correct everywhere, affordable only scoped (34µs/file).
  • D2 internal/sizer is THE size seam: Blocks / UniqueAllocated / FreedByDelete(statfs delta); logical DirSize retired from decision paths — du-fiction is the founding bug.
  • D3 Leak signatures are DATA: #1 chrome-code-sign-clone (lsof-empty staleness — mtime proven unsafe), #2 private-tmp-agent-scratch (24G honest refill) — the two live classes here.
  • D4 /private/ carve-out = parallel predicate: generic CanDelete unchanged; signature-scoped predicate + apply-time lsof recheck — ship the fix without weakening the wall.
  • D5 Offload = per-asset playbooks in 3 classes: native-config (pnpm/colima/claude), relocate move+symlink (blueprints NEVER-delete, vm_bundles), Electron = manual until smoke-proven — every verdict live-proven.
  • D6 Volume-guard law: UUID pin + mount check + LIVE write-probe at plan AND apply — Kompis proves presence ≠ usability.
  • D7 Kompis EXCLUDED as target (corrupt, RO, 17.5G at risk) — surfaced as nn-bl-volume-health.
  • D8 Velocity = light the existing pipeline: cache_roots + two call sites + bytes/day; cadence rides the single-consumer trig channel (the scan-storm guard) — proven one-field fix.
  • D9 0005 not a blocker; READ path is the gap: consolidate DDL, Store methods, stats wired — the trail must become readable for velocity/leak history.
  • D10 Snapshot ghost CLOSED: no TM, zero Data snapshots — ghost = clone du-fiction + refill; snapshot check demoted to backlog diagnostic.
  • D11 Ride existing seams, defer 3-path unification (modules/heuristics/autoclean) — no single choke point exists; unifying first stalls the wins.
  • D12 Wave gate = race gate: CC=/usr/bin/clang go test -race ./... && go vet ./... — Makefile truth; baseline green (dry-run re-proven by Decide, exit 0).
  • D13 Sequenced merges: sizer → leaks → offload; audit-ledger → velocity (import deps + shared main.go/tick.go/report_cmd.go/config.go).
  • D14 Menubar one-click deferred to wave 2 — submenu built-but-disconnected; Wails UI is a different toolchain gate (nn-bl-daemon-leak-alerts, nn-bl-wails-ui).

Wave plan — wave 1 IN FLIGHT (5 slices, all tasks published children of noo-noo-disk-guardian-epic)

All build work in worktrees of /Volumes/SATECHI/github/noo-noo (baseline b6b9644). Gate for every slice: CC=/usr/bin/clang go test -race ./... && CC=/usr/bin/clang go vet ./... (dry-run green before dispatch). Merge order: 1 and 2 in parallel; 3 and 5 after their dependencies; 4 last.

  1. nn-w1-sizer-truth (fable, large) — surface: Go internal/sizer. The truth foundation: st_blocks tier + F_LOG2PHYS_EXT extent-union (pack(4) 20-byte marshal, (st_dev,devoffset) keys) + statfs freed-bytes.
  2. nn-w1-audit-ledger (opus, medium) — surface: store + daemon wiring. auto_clean_events single-sourced in schema.sql; Store methods; stats wired non-nil. Parallel with #1 (disjoint files).
  3. nn-w1-leaks-registry (fable, large) — surface: internal/leaks + safety + CLI. Data-driven registry; Chrome code_sign_clone (lsof-gated) + /private/tmp scratch (age+lsof); /private/ parallel predicate + protective fail-before test; live diagnose-only host scan. AFTER #1 merges.
  4. nn-w1-offload-module (fable, large) — surface: modules/offload + core/volguard + CLI + config. Relocate op + Destination; UUID/write-probe guard; playbooks (pnpm/colima/claude native, blueprints+vm_bundles relocate, blueprints NEVER-delete); home-symlink standing-risk detection. LAST (after #1, #3, #5).
  5. nn-w1-velocity-live (opus, medium) — surface: config + daemon call sites + heuristics. cache_roots lights the pipeline; bytes/day truth; scanCaches on sizer.Blocks; pressure-config dead-wiring fixed. AFTER #2 (+#1) merges.

Backlog filed (published children): nn-bl-daemon-leak-alerts (p1), nn-bl-volume-health (p1 — Kompis corruption is a user-facing data risk), nn-bl-toggle-persist (p2), nn-bl-auto-relocate-gates (p2), nn-bl-home-symlink-guard (p2), nn-bl-wails-ui (p2), nn-bl-action-unify (p3), nn-bl-store-retention (p3), nn-bl-snapshot-signal (p3), nn-bl-disable-class (p3).

DEBRIEF — wave 1 review (2026-07-15, reviewer: Fable, last hands before merge)

What shipped (per slice — final branch = what the lead merges, in this order)

  1. nn-w1-sizer-truth — branch loop-epic/internal-sizer-apfs-truth-sizing-st-bloc-0 (ac77b84, unchanged: review found nothing to fix). Verdict: excellent. The 20-byte pack(4) wire layout is byte-exact-pinned; the live-discovered APFS hole semantic (fcntl SUCCEEDS with devoffset=-1 spanning the hole) is handled and documented; clone/sparse/cross-device/cross-tree/hardlink cases all genuinely tested; cost doctrine (~34µs/file, on-demand only) in the package doc. 16 tests, race-gate green.
  2. nn-w1-audit-ledger — final branch loop-epic/auto-clean-audit-trail-readable-auto-cle-1-r (f0f55fe). Fix: one stale interface doc comment refreshed. Verdict: clean single-sourcing — DDL lives in schema.sql alone (v2), store owns the row types (alias trick dodges the import cycle correctly), the old always-zero Status bug has a real end-to-end regression test against a real store.Open.
  3. nn-w1-leaks-registry — final branch loop-epic/internal-leaks-data-driven-leak-signatur-2-r (0e93232, stacked on sizer ac77b84). Review fixes: (a) categorical leak wall case-folded — APFS is case-insensitive by default, so a misauthored glob like /library/caches/* reached real /Library files past the case-sensitive prefix check; (b) /private/etc/ (the real /etc) added to the categorical blocklist — the /private/ carve-out is for var/folders + tmp leak classes, never system config; both pinned in safety_probe_test.go; (c) leaks listed in top-level CLI usage (was undiscoverable). Verdict: strong — fail-safe lsof probe (timeout/failure ⇒ LIVE), apply-time TOCTOU re-check proven by a test that really holds a file open, generic CanDelete wall untouched and probe-tested.
  4. nn-w1-offload-module — final branch loop-epic/internal-modules-offload-playbook-driven-3-r (6365f5a; contains sizer + leaks-r merges so the train stays conflict-free). Review fixes: (a) wired the sizer — the SizeFns seam defaulted to a clone-blind st_blocks fallback for UniqueAllocated/FreedByDelete because sizer was unmerged at build time; the seam now defaults to sizer.UniqueAllocated (the exact wiring the builder stamped as owed to "the rebase"); (b) resolved the cli.go usage collision between leaks and offload. Verdict: careful where it must be — copy→verify→swap-to-bak→symlink→verify→only-then-drop-bak with restore on failure, UUID+write-probe guard re-run at apply, NeverDelete structural (module knows no delete op), stop-gates injectable and tested.

What stalled and why

nn-w1-velocity-live: 0 commits, honestly held in_progress with all criteria met:false. Its brief required branching after sizer AND audit-ledger were on main — but in a wave where nothing merges until review, that condition can never come true mid-wave. The stall was correct worker behavior and a dispatch-design flaw: a slice hard-dependent on two siblings' merges should be a next-wave slice by construction. Re-dispatch it FIRST next wave, immediately after the merge train.

Cross-slice review

Full integration simulated on a throwaway branch (all four final branches merged onto b6b9644): zero conflicts in the stated order, go test -race + go vet green, gofmt clean. Live diagnose-only smoke on the founding machine: leaks list names the surviving Chrome clone LIVE with the 7-process lsof proof and a 7.7MB du-fiction delta, and age-protects all 9 scratch trees; offload scan reports pnpm 4.3G / colima 13G / .claude 8.3G / blueprints 14.8G / vm_bundles 10G with exact native commands, and flags the unguarded Desktop/Documents/Downloads → SATECHI symlinks. Known residual duplication: offload keeps its own permission-tolerant st_blocks walker (allocatedBlocks) for Blocks because it surfaces a partial+denied error the Scan evidence uses — deliberate, documented in fill().

Ledger audit

No fixes needed — the cleanest ledger this reviewer has audited: all four built slices in_progress with only merge-gate criteria open, every met criterion carrying real run evidence, honest deviation notes (audit-ledger declared its apply.go excursion), velocity's stall stamped with misses and a build-order handoff, 10 backlog children published. Nothing outside the wave was touched.

Grade: A-

Earned by: four slices of genuinely high craft — the sizer alone converts the founding 129G→3G incident into a byte-exact-tested instrument, and every user-facing number in the wave now cites real reclaimable bytes; safety philosophy held everywhere (diagnose-only defaults, fail-safe liveness, structural never-delete, protective baselines); an exemplary honest ledger. Held back from A by: the velocity stall — wish ask #4 ("schedule cleanup based on how fast it clutters") ships nothing this wave, and the miss was predictable at Decide time; the clone-aware wiring gap in offload needed the reviewer to land the epic's own core doctrine in its newest module; and nothing is user-usable until the merge train + a configured [offload] section land.

Next wave

  1. Lead merge train (closes the five merge-gate criteria): sizer → audit-ledger-r → leaks-r → offload-r. Plain merges, this exact order.
  2. Re-dispatch nn-w1-velocity-live — unblocked the moment the train lands; the brief is already perfect.
  3. Make offload real for the user: pin SATECHI (UUID 0DBD1B63-0377-450B-A340-7E72D0925EBC) in [offload], run the three native-config relocations (pnpm/colima/.claude ≈ 25G) and the two guarded relocates (blueprints + vm_bundles ≈ 25G) — this is the wish's actual space relief.
  4. nn-bl-daemon-leak-alerts — the daemon should name the leak within one pressure cycle (the wish's "it doesn't care that I'm deleting" moment).
  5. Then nn-bl-home-symlink-guard / nn-bl-volume-health (Kompis is a standing data risk).

States the direction and the 15-question survey plan.
